findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Bowls and baskets stored along the cookline were observed with the food contact surface faced upward. Discussed with the PIC and items were inverted to correct the violation. Ensure that food contact surfaces are stored in a manner that doesn’t expose the food contact surface to contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Both soda gun nozzles in the bar area were observed soiled with dried liquids. Additionally, the rubber gun holders were also observed soiled. Discussed with the PIC. Ensure that nozzles and gun holders are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent soil accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.11(E) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (E) Except when dry cleaning methods are used as specified under § 4-603.11, surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting FOOD that is not TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cleaned: (1) At any time when contamination may have occurred; (2) At least every 24 hours for iced tea dispensers and CONSUMER self service UTENSILS such as tongs, scoops, or ladles; (3) Before restocking CONSUMER self-service EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS such as condiment dispensers and display containers; and (4) In EQUIPMENT such as ice bins and BEVERAGE dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of EQUIPMENT such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, BEVERAGE and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending EQUIPMENT: (a) At a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or (b) Absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: The bar’s handwashing sink was obstructed with several bar mats. The mats were removed to correct the violation. The PIC mentioned that mats were temporarily placed over the sink. Be sure to keep all handwashing sinks unobstructed so that sinks are accessible at all times for handwashing purposes.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The dish machine in the bar area was tested at 0ppm (CL). The sanitizer bottle was replaced and primed after several cycles before testing at 100ppm (CL). Ensure that dish machines are testing at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration level.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Both soda gun nozzles in the bar area were observed soiled with dried liquids. Additionally, the rubber gun holders were also observed soiled. Shown to the PIC. Ensure that nozzles and gun holders are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent soil accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.11(E) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (E) Except when dry cleaning methods are used as specified under § 4-603.11, surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting FOOD that is not TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cleaned: (1) At any time when contamination may have occurred; (2) At least every 24 hours for iced tea dispensers and CONSUMER self service UTENSILS such as tongs, scoops, or ladles; (3) Before restocking CONSUMER self-service EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS such as condiment dispensers and display containers; and (4) In EQUIPMENT such as ice bins and BEVERAGE dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of EQUIPMENT such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, BEVERAGE and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending EQUIPMENT: (a) At a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or (b) Absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The facility uses a dry and liquid batter for frying meats, seafood, and veggies. The dry batter is replaced every few hours. While the liquid batter is held on an ice bath, the internal temperature was probed at 51F. Ice was only covering the bottom surface of the container. Demonstrated to the kitchen employee how to effectively set up an ice bath to ensure proper cold holding temperatures for time/temperature TCS foods. Be sure that ice covers all outer surfaces of containers to maintain a temperature of 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: None of the employees working at the time of the inspection were certified food protection managers. Discussed the need of having at least one individual who is food manager certified at all times. Ensure that more employees are food manager certified to cover all hours of operations.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: There were sliced tomatoes stored along the serving line that were observed at room temperature. The PIC mentioned that the food items used as toppings are normally cold held over ice to control the safety of the food item. The items include shredded parmesan cheese, sliced tomatoes, cut onions, etc. The items were replaced to correct the violation. Discussed the need to either use temperature control or time control for the sliced tomatoes and Parmesan cheese. Be sure that all employees are on one accord regarding which safety measure is used. If using temperature control, be sure that TCS foods are properly placed on ice so that all sides of the containers are covered. If using time control, be sure that TCS are held for no longer than four hours before being switched.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: There was a jug of pickled products stored inside of the walk in cooler that exceeded the seven day date marking. The mixture included but not limited to cut onions, pickles, and other veggies. The date listed on the jug was 12/15/2025. Discussed that any products pickled in house must not exceed the seven day rule, as they are considered TCS after preparation.  Ensure that pickled items aren’t held longer than seven days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: There were several reduced oxygen packaged salmon stored in the drawer cooler along the cook-line. The salmon packages were thawed and the label mentioned to remove fish from packaging before thawing or keep frozen. The employees were instructed to slice a small opening into the packaging to remove the packed air to correct the violation. Ensure that ROP fish are removed from packaging before thawing occurs if the fish isn't going to be cooked immediately. Thawing food in ROP creates a perfect environment for bacteria to grow.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Several shelves inside the walk in cooler were observed rusted and accumulated with mold debris. Shown to the PIC. No foods in the cooler were uncovered. Ensure that surfaces are cleaned and sanitized as frequent as necessary to prevent buildup and contamination of food items.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Overall, the facility has significant improved with date marking. Staff appear to mostly monitor date marking of TCS foods, however, there were a few items that were past the seven day timeframe (date marked 9/17 and 9/18). These items include buffalo dip, various in house made sauces, sloppy joe, etc. Discussed with PIC and items were discarded. Ensure that any TCS foods that are held in house for longer than seven days are dated marked and discarded if not used within seven days of preparation.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: There were two packages of raw beef thawing at room temperature inside of the triple sink in the kitchen area. Discussed with PIC proper thawing methods. The beefs were placed under running cool water, allowing for the water to cycle and drain off loose particles. When thawing in sinks, ensure that items are placed under running cool water and are completely submerged.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: An insect glue trap was observed hanging from the ceiling in the dish machine area. The glue trap was not directly placed over clean dishes, however, the trap contained a significant amount of dead flies and could possibly contaminate clean dishes during the warewashing process. Ensure that insect traps are placed in areas where food and/or food contact surfaces aren’t exposed to contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (A) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: There is a mini cooler to the left of the of the triple and a drawer cooler in the kitchen area that are no longer in service. The kitchen employees mentioned that the facility has no future plans to use the pieces of equipment. If pieces of equipment aren’t functioning properly and there’s no plan for usage in the future, then be sure to remove equipment from facility, as they can be considered as litter.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Mold was observed on several blackberries stored in containers in the walk in cooler. The moldy blackberries were shown to the PIC and then discarded. PIC mentioned that their food distributor, What Chefs Wants, has delivered moldy product before. Ensure that food is always in good condition and never served moldy.
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: There wasn’t a Certified Food Protection Manager present at the start of the inspection. Shortly afterwards, a CFPM arrived. Ensure that there is a CFPM present all hours of operation. There should be at least 2 employees that are food manager certified.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12(A) Observed staff to don gloves without handwashing. Tasks were being changed and hair was touched. Discussed hand washing during the inspection with multiple staffers. Facility may benefit from revisiting hand washing as part of the onboarding education for new employees. See that hands are washed when changing tasks and at any other appropriate time. 


Cleaning Procedure. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands or arms for at least 20 seconds, using a cleaning compound in a HANDWASHING SINK that is equipped as specified under § 5-202.12 and Subpart 6-301.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11(B) Observed an employee handling raw red onion that will not have a cook step prior to use with bare hands. Without provocation, employee donned gloves. Educated staff on proper hand washing and glove use. Make sure that gloves are always worn when handling ready-to-eat foods. 

Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Kitchen hand sink was noted as not having paper towels available at the start of the inspection. Paper toweling was never provided during the inspection despite having several conversations related to hand washing and providing proper tools for hand washing. The facility will provide paper toweling prior to SCDPH leaving. Discussed hand washing and insuring sinks are supplied. 

Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(C) There is observed a sani-bucket on the cookline with 0ppm Quat. The bucket was from the morning and despite only being used once, the chemical was out of solution. Discussed monitoring sani-buckets and insuring that chemical for sani-cloths is available as one of the first steps during opening or restocking the kitchen. The facility should store all wiping cloths in a chemical solution between uses to prevent bacterial growth. Discussed with multiple staffers. Bucket was emptied and refilled during the inspection. 


 Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) The baffle of the ice machine in the kitchen is observed soiled. See that the ice machine baffle is cleaned and sanitized.

The following food contact surfaces were observed soiled with dried food debris:
- Can opener
- Meat slicer and Fry cutter
Discussed and shown to kitchen employee and surfaces were placed in the dish machine to be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned after each use to prevent build-up on food contact surfaces. 

Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Sliced tomatoes stored in an ice bath were probed at 55F. Discussed proper ice bath techniques with kitchen employees and more ice was added to the pan. There must be enough ice to cover all outer sides of containers that store food. Ensure that ice baths are sufficient enough to maintain proper cold holding temperatures (41F or less) for TCS food items.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17(B)  The facility is inconsistently date marking foods. Several of the foods were labeled with the creation date and others were dated with the discard date. Staff needs to be consistent with their practices. See that everyone is educated on using the date of creation AND discarding within seven days (if created on 2/20 then used or discarded by the end of 2/26 - Day one is day of creation). 
Educate staff on the system for date marking. 
Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17(B) Several foods are observed with dates from January and early February. Several of these containers (garlic butter) are fairly full and have likely been recently created. Discussed removing old date labels prior to washing. See that dish staff knows to remove the tape holding dates prior to ware washing. Foods held longer than seven days were discarded. 

Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
7-201.11 Separation. Observed a container of oven cleaner stored over plates, pans, and bulk container of salt. Removed to floor during inspection. Also, observed a can of glass cleaner stored over the ice bin. Cleaner was moved to floor during the inspection. See that chemicals are stored so they will not spill onto food and food equipment. 


 Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The ambient temperature of the walk in cooler was observed at 45F. Discussed having the walk in cooler serviced due to alarming ambient temperature. The ambient temperature of cold holding equipment should be 41F or less. Ensure that cold holding equipment is capable of maintaining proper cold holding temperatures . Will follow-up on 3/7/2025.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.11(A) Observed a screw within the ice machine to be starting to rust and discolor the interior bin of the ice machine. Replace the screw to prevent potential cross-contamination. 
There is water observed at the base of the preparation cooler across from the grill line. See that equipment is maintained to prevent ponding water. 
Finally, there is a missing cover on the ice machine in the kitchen that should cover some of the mechanisms and would allow for easier cleaning. See that the missing panel on the right side of the ice machine is replaced. 

 Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(B) The facility has recently created a daily chore chart that is being executed daily. There are still several surfaces that would benefit from more consistent cleaning: 1) the back of the lid of the preparation cooler across from the cookline; 2) underneath the flat top/grill top; 3)


Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Observed the floors, walls, and ceilings throughout the facility to need cleaning. There is grease accumulating in the corner by the gas canisters to the left of the cookline. The floor in the walk-in cooler is thickly coated with soil beneath the conduit lines. There is dust observed in-front of the fans of the walk-in cooler. The wall by the left side of the cookline has dust hanging from the surface. The baffles of the hood are just starting to show some signs of accumulation and the wall behind the cookline is coated with food splash. Be sure to thoroughly clean around and underneath kitchen equipment when cleaning occurs at night.  

Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.110 Observed personal beverages being stored atop the preparation cooler. One was a cup with a lid and straw, the other a closed container. The cup was discarded. Store beverages so that if they fall, there is no potential for cross contamination. 

 Using Dressing Rooms and Lockers. (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment:
Mold was observed on several blackberries stored in containers in the walk in cooler. The moldy blackberries were shown to the PIC and then discarded. PIC mentioned that their food distributor, Sysco, has delivered moldy product before. Ensure that food is always in good condition and never served moldy. 

Several containers of blackberries were observed to be moldy in the walk in cooler.
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized

Ensure that soda guns and the can opener are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent accumulation. 

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
A wet mop head was observed to be stored inside of a mop bucket. Discussed with PIC and mop was repositioned. Ensure that mop heads are stored in a manner that allows them to air dry properly. 

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Observed fruit flies underneath and around the dish machine in the dish area. PIC mentioned that the facility is in the process of repairing the wall behind the dish machine due to water damage from a bursted pipe. PIC also mentioned that the repairs will be occurring in the next couple of weeks. Ensure that the facility is free of any insects. 

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The dish machine’s sanitizer concentration was tested at 0ppm (CL). The sanitizer jug appeared to be empty and was switched out by an employee. The machine was tested again to have a 100ppm concentration. Ensure that the dish machine’s sanitizer concentration is maintained at 100ppm (CL) to sanitize dishes properly. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
TCF food items stored in the drawer coolers were tempting between 76F-80F. PIC mentioned that the circuit breaker that provides power to the cooler had popped. The TCS food items include but aren't limited to salmon, pork, cooked noodles, and cooked vegetables. All food items stored in the cooler were discarded and power was provided to the cooler. Be sure that TCS foods are maintained at 41F or below to ensure proper cold holding temperatures. 

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Observed fruit flies underneath and around the dish machine in the dish area. PIC mentioned that the facility is in the process of repairing the wall behind the dish machine due to water damage from a bursted pipe. Pest control provides service to the facility four times a month. Ensure that the facility is free of any insects. Will follow up on 10/8/2024. 

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed a mop head stored in an empty mop bucket. Discussed proper storage for mop heads with PIC. Ensure that mop heads are stored in a position that allows for them to air dry properly. 

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
There wasn’t a CFPM present at the start of the inspection. A CFPM arrived shortly afterwards. Ensure that CFPMs are present to cover all hours of operation. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the inside of the ice machine in the bar area to be soiled with mold. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that the inside of the ice machine is cleaned as frequent as necessary in order to prevent mold buildup. 

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed several TCS food items (cheeses and diced tomatoes products) to have internal temperatures between 54F-57F probed. The food items were placed in an ice bath and PIC noted that the items had been in the ice bath sine 11am. Items were discarded. Ensure that TCF foods are maintained at a temperature of 41F or less. 

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed mozzarella cheeses and chicken to not be date marked in the cooler across from the fryers. Discussed with PIC and items were date marked with the appropriate opening date. PIC noted that items were opened the day before. Ensure that TCS food held in house longer than 24 hours are date marked and discarded if not used within 7 days of opening. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Observed boxes of drinking straws to be stored on the floor in the bar area. Discussed with PIC and straws were removed from the floor. Ensure that all single service items are stored off the floor and in a manner that prevents them from contamination. 

4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Overall, the floors throughout the kitchen were soiled with food debris and grease. Ensure that floors throughout the kitchen including underneath equipment are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent buildup. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after cleaning.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Observed personal beverages in coolers mixed with food intended for public consumption. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that personal items are stored in a designated place separate from food or drinks that are going to be sold to the public. 

6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.
